page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v6 is an Edsv6-family virtual machine configured with 96 vCPUs and 768.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 48 physical cores, it operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, featuring a 260 MB L3 cache and support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Local storage is bundled, consisting of 5669 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in several categories. The system achieved a Passmark CPU score of 93,126.45 and demonstrated top-tier capabilities in CPU extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with uncached read-only large block speeds reaching 506.7 GB/sec and write speeds at 207.77 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. Database operations on Passmark scored 35,335.9, and Redis SET operations reached 122.52 million operations per second. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,410.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 87,583.29.

While single-core performance benchmarks like stress-ng and gzip compression fall into the average tier, the high core count and memory density offset this for parallelized workloads. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density of 768 GB RAM and over 5.6 TB of local NVMe SSD storage provides a consolidated platform for memory-intensive and storage-heavy deployments without requiring external disk attachments. This server is suited for large-scale database operations, memory-cached applications, software compilation, and medium-to-large LLM inference tasks where prompt processing speeds remain strong.
